content.prompt: Sketch these parabolas by taking out a common factor, then CTS. Show vertex and intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(x^2+2x-5)\\y&=2(x^2+2x+1-1-5)\\y&=2((x+1)^2-6)\\y&=2(x+1)^2-12\end{aligned}$$
Since $a=2>0$, the parabola is concave up.

For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(0+1)^2-12\\y&=-10\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercepts, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}2(x+1)^2-12&=0\\(x+1)^2&=6\\x+1&=\pm\sqrt6\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt6\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(-1,-12)$.

$$\begin{aligned}y&=3(x^2-4x+3)\\y&=3(x^2-4x+4-4+3)\\y&=3((x-2)^2-1)\\y&=3(x-2)^2-3\end{aligned}$$
Since $a=3>0$, the parabola is concave up.

For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=3(0-2)^2-3\\y&=9\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercepts, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3(x-2)^2-3&=0\\(x-2)^2&=1\\x-2&=\pm1\\x&=2\pm1\\x&=1\text{ or }3\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(2,-3)$.

Since $a=2>0$, the parabola is concave up.

For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(0-3)^2-32\\y&=-14\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercepts, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}2(x-3)^2-32&=0\\(x-3)^2&=16\\x-3&=\pm4\\x&=3\pm4\\x&=-1\text{ or }7\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(3,-32)$.

Since $a=4>0$, the parabola is concave up.

For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=4(0+2)^2-40\\y&=-24\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercepts, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}4(x+2)^2-40&=0\\(x+2)^2&=10\\x+2&=\pm\sqrt{10}\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}$$
